listings.title: West 1077 Ranch
listings.types_label: Farms and Ranches, Recreational Property, Hunting Property
listings.description_short: Nestled on 227.379 acres just minutes from Bandera, the West 1077 Ranch awaits the next chapter in its storied history. Perfectly suited as a Hill Country corporate retreat, event venue, multi-generational family compound or scenic rural destination,
listings.description_full: Nestled on 227.379 acres just minutes from Bandera, the West 1077 Ranch awaits the next chapter in its storied history. Perfectly suited as a Hill Country corporate retreat, event venue, multi-generational family compound or scenic rural destination, the ranchs rustic charm invites guests to slow down and savor the beautiful, gently rolling Hill Country landscape. Located within an hour of San Antonio, the ranch fronts on Bandera Creek Road and abuts the Hill Country State Natural Area, one of the states most beautiful hidden gems.,,Having the 5,300-acre Hill Country State Natural Area as a neighbor expands the opportunity for outdoor adventure. Landowners sharing a boundary fence that has an existing gate with the natural area can arrange private-gate access, giving family, friends and guests entre to the beloved park and its miles of trails suitable for horseback riding, biking, hiking and bird watching. The nature areas presence also provides insurance against future development, keeping the neighborhood wild.,,Stands of oaks are scattered across the hills. Native grass, shrubs and prickly pear lend interest and nutrition for passing wildlife. Thanks to its gentle topography, the land has several suitable building sites if more facilities or amenities are desired. ,,Trails, ideal for horseback riding, hiking or biking, crisscross the ranch. A wet weather pond could be developed into year-round water feature. Hills and valleys create a scenic backdrop for life outdoors. Sunrises, sunsets and the inky, star-filled skies are ever-changing masterpieces worthy of daily admiration and contemplation.,,With 13 comfortable cabins, the turn-key ranch retreat can accommodate up to 63 guests overnight. The simple, clean accommodations radiate warmth because of the golden-hued wood throughout. The furniture, much of which is crafted from peeled cedar logs, adds solidity and the flavor of the Old West.,,Other lodging options include a 2-bedroom/1-bath, farmhouse-style cottage with an open kitchen/dining/living area and an inviting front porch with rocking chairs. Guests can also stay in the one-bedroom apartment with a full kitchen and bath that is attached to the Sunflower House Assembly Hall. ,,With its light-filled rooms and contemporary feel, the 3-bedroom/2-bath owners farmhouse stands in contrast to the rusticity of most of the facilities. The open floor plan encompasses a sleek modern kitchen and living room with a fireplace, a dining room and well-sited French doors that open to a wraparound deck overlooking the valley and into the hills. Other features include a well-appointed master suite and laundry room.,,West 1077 Ranch also boasts a lodge outfitted with a large, well-equipped commercial kitchen and an expansive front porch with plenty of rocking chairs for soaking up the views and enjoying the company of fellow nature lovers. The lodge is also home to a dining hall designed to efficiently handle large crowds at mealtimes and a gathering area that beckons guests to linger before or after meals.,,The recently updated Sunflower House serves as an assembly hall that seats up to 90 participants for corporate presentations, breakout sessions, workshops or other events. The combination of the ranchs fiber optic system and a simple AV set up allows video meetings and webinars to be simultaneously broadcast and recorded. The hall has restrooms and a nearby laundry shed makes clean up easy.,,An office, a second laundry with two washers and dryers, a pump house and an assortment of outbuildings round out the infrastructure.,,To maximize fun in the country, West 1077 Ranch is ready for horses. The barn features 13 stalls, three outdoor pens and an outdoor arena. Trail riding on the ranch as well as on the adjoining natural area, could be a favorite pastime. Guests will enjoy splashing in the outdoor pool, measuring about 35 x 17 and ranging in depth from 3 feet to 6 feet, and the adjoining deck with a Tiki Bar, sunshades and lounge chairs.,,Three wells and two cisterns, with a collective capacity of 12,000 gallons, supply the water for the ranch. In addition, the owners house and cottage are outfitted with water catchment systems to make the most of the rain that falls for domestic uses. Both homes are also serviced by well water.,,Because connectivity is a must, the ranch is equipped with four fiber optic modems and routers as well as an ORBI Mesh WiFi extender system that provides reception in all buildings. One of the newest upgrades is an electric car charging station at the lodge.,,For those who want to explore beyond the ranch gate, adventure awaits nearby. Bandera, known as the Cowboy Capital of the World, is just 10 miles away and home to a charming Main Street, boutique shopping, and restaurants, all served up with Western flair. Summer is book-ended with annual rodeos on Memorial Day and Labor Day.,,Lost Maples State Natural Area, home to Texas most splendid fall colors and one of the states most popular outdoor destinations, is less than hour away. Fredericksburg, arguably one of Texas most beloved towns, which is known for its German history and burgeoning wine industry, is just an hour northeast of the ranch. ,,West 1077 Ranch is a storied gathering place with a bold past and a bright future. Imagine writing the next chapter for the ranchand for yourself.,,Contact Conner W. Hood, Broker Associate, at (830) 928-2317. Listed for $4,750,000.

listings.description_short: JUST REDUCED! Exceptional live water ranch with frontage on three (3) creeks, two (2) of which originate on the ranch. Extremely rare feature! ACREAGE. 430+/- Acres LAND TYPE. Texas Hill Country, Live Water, Hunting and Recreation, Full-Time, Weekend
listings.description_full: JUST REDUCED!,Exceptional live water ranch with frontage on three (3) creeks, two (2) of which originate on the ranch. Extremely rare feature!,,ACREAGE.  430+/- Acres,,LAND TYPE.  Texas Hill Country, Live Water, Hunting and Recreation, Full-Time, Weekend or Seasonal,,TAX EXEMPTION.  1-d-1 Agriculture Use Tax Exemption,,LOCATION.  Maple Springs Ranch is almost centrally located between Vanderpool and Medina.     ,11+/- miles west of Medina (15 minutes) ; 15+/- miles east of Vanderpool (20 minutes) ; 1.5+/- hours northwest of San Antonio ; 2.75+/- hours southwest of Austin ; 4.5+/- hours west of Houston ; 5.5+/- hours southwest of Dallas  ,,ACCESS.  Paved and renowned farm to market road 337 leads to all-weather county maintained Elam Creek Road from either direction coming from Medina or Vanderpool. Recent ranch road work and clearing has been done to access points of the ranch from one end to the other.    , ,LAND.  Land that literally takes your breath away and is a breath of fresh air at the same time. ,	   ,Maple Springs Ranch is the epitome of sprawling Texas hill country acreage. Exciting ranges in elevation and panoramic displays of the Bandera Canyonlands. A little bit of everything... Once again, let us emphasize...THREE (3) impressively STRONG flowing creeks, a super rare quality and incomparable feature. Rock bottom creek beds, level and rolling bottomlands, rising mountain walls, canyons, valleys, ravines, grottos, boulders and exposed tree roots that give this ranch the same vibe as some of the most renowned state parks in Texas. And with much of the ranch undisturbed for many moons, from the low points of the ranch to the high points, who knows what kind of geological formations or artifacts are on the ranch or if there are any caves awaiting exploration. Bring out your inner adventurous self and take this ranch on for all its got to offer.,,WATER.  Three spring-fed creeks characterized by stone bottom terrain. As it flows downstream, it traverses through slopes, stones and limestone benches, creating scattered cascades of small waterfalls. The surface water is the upmost excellent water source for free roaming wildlife. 	     ,ELAM CREEK can be found at the front of the ranch.,SLIM CREEK can be found at the center of the ranch.,BAUERLINE CREEK can be found at the back of the ranch.,,LIVE SPRINGS.  During our tour of the ranch, we counted at least 7 springs and lets just say we didn't hike every inch of the ranch. How many springs could there be in total? That would be quite an adventure for the thrill seeker. Figure out the reason behind why these three spring-fed creeks haven't gone dry... not even through the severe Texas droughts we've been experiencing. Now, if you ask us, thats some strong water!  ,,WILDLIFE.  Undisturbed canyon territory can only mean one thing... who knows what is lurking through the ranch. It is known that whitetail, hog and turkey are native to the area. Every now and then a surprising site of enormous red deer or an occasional exotic thats escaped from neighboring ranches over the years. Abundant variety of woodland birds, song birds and rare sightings of migrating waterfowl.,,VEGETATION.  The deep canyons, cool temperatures and moist environment enable native hardwoods and plants to flourish. Maple Springs is speckled with shades of golds, reds, oranges, yellows and vibrant variations of green tones offering some of the most scenic landscape in the Texas hill country. The ranch land and canyons are dominated with Maple trees, Spanish Oak, Linden trees, Pecan, Live Oak, Sycamore, Mountain Laurel and many more... Limestone creek beds and river ledges are landscaped with a mix of creeping vines, wild evergreen southern shield and maidenhead fern species.,,SOILS.  The majority of the ranch is based with Eckrant-Rock outcrop, while the lower portions and narrow valleys have Krum-plately association which consist of clayey sediments.  Good for recreation, woodland, wildlife food and cover. ,,POWER.  Power is on the ranch.,,IMPROVEMENTS.  ,TWO STORY COUNTRY HOME: 3 Bedroom - 2 Bathroom with Fireplace	       ,THE BARN: Equipment and storage barn painted to match the home.,,NOTES.  Its a mystery beyond the Maples!,Tucked deep into the valleys of the canyons you sense a different environment entirely. You SEE beauty in the lands forestry and natural water sources. You HEAR the sounds of silence and nature as you stand in the heart of the ranch beating with strong cool springs and creeks. You FEEL a slight drop in the temperature drawn from the shades of the encompassing mountain walls. You SMELL the crisp freshness in the unpolluted air. And TASTE... well, go ahead, taste the water straight from the headsprings, right out of the ground. Bring your cup and fill it up! ,	   ,Maple Springs features big Texas views and at least two prime sites for building an extravagant dream home or a quaint log cabin or two.   ,,Elevations on the ranch peak at just over  2,100 ft, lending Maple Springs Ranch a front row seat to some of the most scenic views throughout the Texas hill country and Bandera Canyonlands.   , 	   ,MOST UNIQUE FEATURES OF THIS LIVE WATER RANCH.  Boasting numerous live springs and three (3) creeks, which if added up together, totals over a mile of strong flowing crystal clear creek frontage, not to mention, thats BOTH sides ownership on all three (3) creeks...Nuff said!,,,*Information is believed reliable but is not guaranteed by REALTOR. Property is subject to prior sale, correction or withdrawal without notice.

listings.description_short: 1872 +- Acres - Paisano Ranch Utopia - Bandera County Located between Utopia and Tarpley, one of the most desirable and unspoiled areas of the Texas Hill Country, this awesome new listing is one of the most scenic and turnkey ranches available in the
listings.description_full: 1872 +- Acres - Paisano Ranch ,      Utopia - Bandera County,Located between Utopia and Tarpley, one of the most desirable and unspoiled areas of the Texas Hill Country, this awesome new listing is one of the most scenic and turnkey ranches available in the area. The ranch is just minutes south of FM 470 in the heart of the beautiful Seco Creek Valley, just minutes from Utopia, 30 minutes to Bandera and an hour to San Antonio and Kerrville. Other nearby attractions are Lost Maples Park, Garner State Park and the ever popular Frio River. ,     The ranch offers all new game proof fencing, soft release pens, electric gate access, a 3 bedroom home with concrete drive, 2 car garage, wood rail fenced yard, large patio, garden area, manicured lawn, large healthy Oaks and extensive landscaping around the home. The ranch offers a second home that is 4 bedrooms and serves a lodge for hunters and guests. Both homes have recently remodeled with new paint, new flooring throughout, new appliances, new central A/C units, new hot water heaters and other upgrades., Other improvements at the lodge/headquarters include:,20'x20' covered game cleaning building with hoist, sink and cleaning area. 30'x40' metal equipment building with walk in cooler, ice storage and firewood rack., An insulated drive through 40'x50' metal shop with full length workbench, roll up doors and serves as equipment storage area. ,30'x 75' covered equipment barn with 3 bays for parking and storing ranch equipment and rail container.  ,The shop and equipment barn have been equipped with a rain collection system that feeds water to a new Pioneer 30,000 gallon metal storage tank. ,A newly drilled Trinity well with 1200 gallon concrete storage tank provides water to the home, pens, pond and several water stations. ,An electrical power line runs completely through the ranch from north to south. Phone and high speed internet service is in place at both homes. ,,        The ranch consists of two long parallel valleys with over a dozen feeder canyons, offers the near perfect mix of level to sloping bottom land, spring fed canyons, deep fertile bottoms with adequate soils for cultivating hay or food plots, steep majestic hardwood lined hills, limestone bluffs with sheer outcroppings and wide open valleys covered in huge Live Oaks. The deep canyons are home to Spanish Oak, Blue Oak, Cedar Elms, Wild Cherry, Madrone, Sumac, Persimmon and Sycamore. Huge stands of Sycamore line the once live creeks indicating there is still ample subsurface water in each valley for the potential for pond and lake development. ,     The current owner has developed the ranch to be a Whitetail Deer hunting destination with genetically improved and intensively managed deer herd producing trophy deer. Forty bred whitetail does and two breeder bucks were released on the ranch in 2023, with young trophy bucks already scoring in the 170 range. There are multiple bulk feed stations throughout the ranch and 6 strategically placed hunting blinds and spin cast feeders set up to accommodate hunters. ,,    One of the highlights of the ranch is the exceptional interior road system the owners have created over many years that provides easy access to virtually every part of the ranch.  Most of the ranch is easily accessible by 2 WD vehicle and a single tour of the 16+ miles of road system is like a safari, offering a buyer breathtaking views of the Ranch, the Seco Valley, Cascade Valley and hundreds of square miles of the surrounding Hill Country. Words and pictures do not come close. Few ranches offer an interior road system that compares to this ranch. Additionally, the owners have selectively cleared large amounts of Cedar from the property, providing excellent habitat for the large numbers of Whitetail, Turkey, Hogs, Aoudad and many species of Birds and Varmits. The extensive Cedar clearing on the property has made it one of the cleanest ranches available.     ,,      This is a rare opportunity for a buyer to purchase an exceptional Hill Country ranch that has all the features that make this area so special.,Wont last, call Morris Killough    210-415-9850

listings.description_short: Nestled in the heart of the Texas Hill Country, the 134.31 acre Burr Oak Creek Ranch is a rare offering that combines year-round live water, dramatic bluffs, and abundant free-range wildlife in one of the most desirable areas of the state. With 3,400
listings.description_full: Nestled in the heart of the Texas Hill Country, the 134.31 acre Burr Oak Creek Ranch is a rare offering that combines year-round live water, dramatic bluffs, and abundant free-range wildlife in one of the most desirable areas of the state. With 3,400 feet of live-water frontage on Burr Oak Creek, an additional spring-fed ravine spanning 2,100 feet, and striking elevation changes up to 120 feet, the ranch is a showcase of Hill Country beauty.,,Location,Burr Oak Creek Ranch enjoys a prime position between Fredericksburg and Kerrville, two of the regions most vibrant Hill Country communities. The ranch provides a balance of privacy and accessibility while being just minutes from world-class amenities, dining, and entertainment.,,Proximity to Towns / Cities:,  Fredericksburg, TX  16 miles,  Kerrville, TX  14 miles,  San Antonio, TX  60 miles,  Austin, TX  90 miles,,The location also places the ranch within close reach of the renowned 290 Wine Corridor, boutique shopping, and the cultural experiences that make Gillespie and Kerr counties some of the most sought-after in Texas.,,Landscape,Burr Oak Creek Ranch is defined by its scenic terrain and diverse hardwood cover. Towering pecan trees, live oaks, post oaks, and cedar elms dominate the landscape, with minimal cedar presence throughout the property. The ranchs 120 feet of elevation change creates dramatic bluff vistas overlooking Burr Oak Creek, while fertile bottomland and hardwood groves provide shade, character, and excellent habitat for wildlife. This combination of topography and tree cover delivers both functionality and aesthetic appeal, offering prime building sites and endless recreational exploration.,,Water Features,The crown jewel of Burr Oak Creek Ranch is its live-water resources, which are increasingly rare in the Hill Country. The property includes:,  3,400 feet of live-water Burr Oak Creek frontage,  2,100 feet of spring-fed ravine with multiple year-round springs,  Opportunities for future pond and lake development,,The flowing surface water not only enhances the natural beauty of the ranch but also adds recreational and investment value. Whether fishing, swimming, or simply enjoying the serenity of a shaded creekside, the water features make Burr Oak Creek Ranch an elite recreational destination.,,Improvements,Burr Oak Creek Ranch is ready for immediate enjoyment and future development. With paved road frontage and on-site electricity, the property is primed for a new owners vision. Sensible restrictions are in place to help preserve the integrity and quality of the property, ensuring that future improvements align with the natural beauty and long-term value of the ranch. Whether you envision a primary homestead, a luxury retreat, or a recreational getaway, the ranch provides the essential infrastructure for a seamless transition into Texas ranch ownership.,,Wildlife,The ranch is home to a thriving population of native and exotic wildlife, creating year-round opportunities for hunting, photography, and wildlife observation. Species on the property include:,  Whitetail deer,  Turkey,  Hogs,  Axis deer,  Sika deer,  Red stag,  Blackbuck,  Aoudad,The diversity and abundance of free-range exotics, paired with native game, make Burr Oak Creek Ranch one of the most unique and wildlife-rich properties in the region. The ranch carries an agricultural exemption.,,Summary,Burr Oak Creek Ranch represents a rare chance to acquire a legacy-quality Hill Country property with year-round live water, diverse terrain, and rich wildlife populations  all within minutes of Fredericksburg and Kerrville. The unique combination of Burr Oak Creek frontage, spring-fed water sources, dramatic bluffs, free-ranging exotics, and sensible restrictions sets this property apart as both an exceptional recreational retreat and a long-term investment.,,Contact Texas Landmen for more information on this rare offering  opportunities like Burr Oak Creek Ranch do not come around often.

listings.description_full: Located just minutes from Boerne, Texas, this 638 acre ranch provides all the natural attributes which has made the Hill Country a popular destination.  The ranch is characterized by its majestic hills offering breathtaking views and its succulent valleys with numerous springs and the head waters of Privilege Creek. listings.description_full: Welcome to Iron Rapids Ranch, a truly extraordinary live-water retreat nestled along one of the most coveted stretches of the Guadalupe River in the Texas Hill Country. Encompassing approximately 43 acres just outside Boerne, this remarkable property blends timeless natural beauty with thoughtful improvements, fertile land, and the kind of river frontage that generations spend a lifetime searching for.,,Named for the gentle rapids that dance across limestone shelves beneath towering cypress canopies, Iron Rapids Ranch is more than a place to ownit is a place to belong. Here, children swing from rope swings into cool river pools, grandchildren chase fireflies beneath ancient trees, and evenings unfold slowly on the porch as the sounds of rushing water echo through the valley.,,Properties like this rarely become available. Combining over 800+/- feet of pristine Guadalupe River frontage, a custom-built residence, productive soils, and a premier Boerne location, Iron Rapids Ranch offers a lifestyle defined by both refinement and authenticity.,,Location,Ideally situated at 214 Marquardt Road, Iron Rapids Ranch enjoys an exceptional location in one of the Hill Country's most desirable corridors.,,The ranch is located approximately:,11 miles from Boerne,35 miles from Fredericksburg,30 miles from San Antonio,90 miles from Austin,,Boerne has long been regarded as one of Texas' most charming Hill Country communities. Its historic Main Street is lined with locally owned boutiques, art galleries, wine bars, and chef-driven restaurants that make an evening in town feel both sophisticated and unhurried. Fredericksburg's renowned wineries and tasting rooms lie just beyond, while San Antonio offers world-class dining, healthcare, and private aviation access.,,Despite its convenience, Iron Rapids Ranch feels worlds away from city life. Once inside the gate, the pace shifts. The stars burn brighter, mornings arrive more quietly, and the river becomes your daily companion.,,Landscape,The landscape at Iron Rapids Ranch is as functional as it is beautiful. Fertile sandy loam soils support lush coastal fields, established orchard areas, and productive gardens, while mature hardwoods frame the property's edges with shade and privacy.,,Towering cypress treessome centuries oldstand guard along the Guadalupe, their roots gripping the limestone banks just as they have for generations. Their massive branches create cathedral-like canopies over the water, filtering sunlight into dancing reflections that move across the river's surface.,,The property is entirely high fenced, allowing for livestock management, agricultural pursuits, or even the cultivation of a carefully managed exotic game program. Improved coastal fields provide grazing opportunities, while thoughtfully designed irrigation systems support orchards, gardens, and landscape improvements.,Long before modern settlement, these river corridors served as lifelines for the Tonkawa, Lipan Apache, and Comanche peoples who traveled and hunted throughout the Hill Country. Later, German settlers were drawn to these same fertile valleys, establishing the ranching traditions and enduring communities that still define the region today.,,Improvements,Built in 2019, the custom residence at Iron Rapids Ranch was thoughtfully designed to celebrate the surrounding landscape. Offering approximately 2,539+/- square feet of living space, the home embraces an open-concept floor plan filled with natural light and framed by expansive windows that invite the outdoors in.,The residence features three bedrooms, two bathrooms, and an attached three-car garage. Warm finishes and timeless Hill Country design elements create a space that feels equally suited for elegant entertaining and relaxed family weekends.,,Morning coffee naturally drifts onto the porch as mist rises from the river below, while evenings are spent gathered with friends after days on the water.,Additional improvements include a workshop and carport originally designed for woodworking and equipment storage, an implement shed conveniently located near the orchard, full RV hookups for extended guests, and extensive drip irrigation systems servicing both the orchard and high-fenced garden areas.,The ranch was intentionally developed with sustainability and self-sufficiency in mind, creating opportunities for orchards, gardens, greenhouses, poultry operations, beekeeping, and livestock.,,A dependable private water well services the improvements and supports the property's long-term functionality.,,Water Features,The Guadalupe River is unquestionably the crown jewel of Iron Rapids Ranch.,,With approximately 800+/- feet of private frontage, the river here is both intimate and dramatic. A graceful bend creates constantly changing perspectives while natural limestone shelves produce the soft rapids that inspired the ranch's name.,,Massive cypress trees shade deep swimming holes and gentle entry points ideal for children and grandchildren. Mornings begin with casting a fly beneath the overhanging branches. Afternoons invite kayaking, tubing, or simply drifting with the current beneath blue Hill Country skies.,,As evening settles in, the river becomes something entirely differenta soundtrack to dinner on the porch, laughter around the firepit, and quiet conversations carried by the breeze.,Permanent, accessible, and profoundly beautiful, this stretch of the Guadalupe represents an increasingly rare and irreplaceable asset.,,Wildlife,Iron Rapids Ranch supports a thriving population of Hill Country wildlife.,Whitetail deer move through the coastal fields during the early mornings and evenings, while turkey roam beneath the hardwoods and dove fill the skies throughout the seasons. Native songbirds flourish along the river corridor, adding movement and sound to the landscape year-round.,,The high-fenced perimeter also creates flexibility for controlled grazing programs or the establishment of a carefully managed exotic herd.,Whether observing wildlife from the porch or introducing the next generation to the outdoors, the ranch offers endless opportunities to connect with the natural world.,,Summary,Iron Rapids Ranch represents an increasingly rare opportunity to own a legacy-quality Guadalupe River property in one of the Texas Hill Country's most desirable locations.,,Combining over 800+/- feet of spectacular river frontage, fertile and productive land, a beautifully crafted custom residence, thoughtful infrastructure, and proximity to Boerne, Fredericksburg, San Antonio, and Austin, the ranch strikes a remarkable balance between sophistication and authenticity.,This is a place where bare feet replace busy schedules, where the river dictates the rhythm of the day, and where memories are measured not by calendars, but by summers spent on the Guadalupe.,,For those seeking a refined Hill Country retreat capable of becoming a family legacy for generations to come, Iron Rapids Ranch stands among the finest live-water offerings available today.

listings.description_full: Description: Cypress Island Ranch is a beautiful blank-canvas property located in a highly desirable area with excellent long-term upside. Offering strong future development potential while remaining well-suited for recreational and hunting use, this ranch presents a rare opportunity to own a diverse and scenic Hill Country holding.,,The property features approximately 1,700 feet of highly sought-after Cypress Creek frontage, lined with mature, towering cypress trees that create a stunning natural centerpiece. Gently rolling hills, quality native tree cover, and open vistas provide multiple ideal homesites and scenic viewpoints throughout the ranch. With minimal improvements already in place, Cypress Island Ranch is ready for a new owner to shape into a dream property.,,Improvements: Cypress Island Ranch offers a well-designed internal road system, including a concrete creek crossing that allows reliable access across the property. The ranch is low-fenced along the perimeter, with a working water well and electricity available throughout, providing a solid foundation for future improvements.,,Vegetation & Terrain: The ranch is predominantly covered in Live Oak and Post Oak, with selective clearing having been thoughtfully completed to enhance wildlife habitat and overall aesthetics. Strategic cedar coverage remains to provide shelter for wildlife, and multiple improved food plots are in place. The gently rolling terrain creates attractive elevation changes and long views across the property.,,Wildlife: Cypress Island Ranch includes 7 watering and feed stations to supports a strong native whitetail deer herd and a healthy population of Rio Grande turkey. 5 manicured upland bird hunting fields have been established on the property. Additional wildlife includes dove, quail, hogs, and other native species, making this an excellent recreational and hunting property.,,Water: The property is traversed by Cypress Creek, which typically provides strong water flow in normal rainfall years. Combined with the existing water well, the ranch offers reliable water resources for both wildlife and future improvements.,,Minerals: See Broker,,Taxes: Wildlife Exempt - +-$150,,School: Johnson City ISD

A few strides away will find you at the bunkhouse with an office and three one bedroom and one bathroom suites that are perfect for family and friends. The other fantastic improvements include a large shop with a kitchen and one bedroom and bathroom, and the coolest saloon/party barn you will find in this part of the Hill Country. listings.description_short: Cypress River Ranch is a rare 75 acre live-water property set along a premier stretch of the Guadalupe River, offering over 1,325 feet of pristine frontage framed by towering cypress and pecan trees. The combination of clear, flowing water, mature ha
listings.description_full: Cypress River Ranch is a rare 75  acre live-water property set along a premier stretch of the Guadalupe River, offering over 1,325 feet of pristine frontage framed by towering cypress and pecan trees. The combination of clear, flowing water, mature hardwoods, and usable terrain creates a classic Hill Country setting that is increasingly difficult to find.,Beyond its natural beauty, the ranch carries a strong sense of historyboth recent and ancientmaking it more than just a property, but a place with depth, character, and lasting significance.,,Location,Cypress River Ranch is ideally located near Comfort, one of the Hill Countrys most historic and charming communities. The ranch is approximately 20 minutes from Boerne, 45 minutes from San Antonio, and within easy reach of Fredericksburg, placing it in the heart of one of the most desirable regions in Texas.,Access is provided via a private entrance with paved roads, and the property is equipped with underground electricity and fiber, offering modern convenience without compromising the natural setting.,,Landscape,The ranch features a beautiful blend of gently rolling terrain, improved grasses, and mature hardwoods. Heritage oaks surround the homestead, while the river corridor is lined with massive cypress and pecan trees that create shade, privacy, and a striking visual presence.,The land is highly usable, with open pastures suitable for livestock and recreation, complemented by shaded river bottoms that provide a peaceful retreat along the water. This balance of open ground and dense tree cover gives the ranch both functionality and aesthetic appeal.,,Water Features,Water is the cornerstone of Cypress River Ranch. With 1,325  feet of Guadalupe River frontage, the property offers direct access to one of Texas most iconic riversideal for fishing, kayaking, swimming, and relaxing along the banks.,In addition to the river, the ranch includes a a 2.5  acre pond, further enhancing the propertys water resources and recreational value.,The ranch is supported by three water wells, providing strong and reliable water infrastructure for residential, agricultural, and wildlife use.,Improvements,The property is anchored by a charming 1,800  square foot Hill Country home built in the 1950s using classic Sisterdale stone. The residence features three bedrooms and two bathrooms, original wood flooring, a pier-and-beam foundation, and two fireplacesincluding one in the primary bedroom.,Surrounded by large oak trees, the home offers a peaceful and shaded setting, ideal for gatherings or quiet evenings overlooking the land. Several original barns remain in good condition, adding both utility and a sense of history to the ranch.,,History,The Comfort area is rich in Texas history, originally settled by German immigrants in the mid-1800s who were drawn to the regions fertile land and reliable water. The surrounding Hill Country has long been known for its independence, heritage, and connection to the land.,Long before settlement, the area was inhabited by Native American tribes, including groups associated with the regions river systems and abundant natural resources. Evidence of this history can still be found on the ranch today, where arrowheads and other artifacts have been discovered, offering a tangible connection to those who lived on and traveled through this land centuries ago.,,Wildlife,Cypress River Ranch supports a healthy population of native and exotic wildlife, including whitetail deer, axis deer, and turkey. The combination of river frontage, open pasture, and hardwood cover creates an ideal habitat with year-round water and natural forage.,,Build Sites & Use,In addition to the existing improvements, the ranch offers multiple prime build sites throughout the property. Elevated areas provide sweeping views of the surrounding Hill Country, while riverfront locations offer a more private, water-oriented setting.,Whether envisioned as a primary residence, weekend retreat, or legacy family ranch, the property provides flexibility and long-term potential.,,Summary,Cypress River Ranch is a premier 75  acre Guadalupe River property combining exceptional live water, strong infrastructure, and deep historical roots. With over 1,300 feet of river frontage, three water wells, underground utilities, and a prime location near Comfort, Boerne, and Fredericksburg, the ranch represents a rare opportunity to own a meaningful and highly desirable piece of the Texas Hill Country.

listings.title: 320 ac Broken Halos River Ranch
listings.types_label: Recreational Property, Hunting Property
listings.description_short: Tucked deep within one of the most cherished reaches of the Texas Hill Country, where the North Fork headwaters of the Guadalupe River quietly flow, this exceptional riverfront ranch presents a rare opportunity to acquire a thoughtfully improved, hig
listings.description_full: Tucked deep within one of the most cherished reaches of the Texas Hill Country, where the North Fork headwaters of the Guadalupe River quietly flow, this exceptional riverfront ranch presents a rare opportunity to acquire a thoughtfully improved, highly accessible sanctuary of enduring quality. Known locally as The Flats, the property is defined by an expansive limestone riverbed that stretches gracefully under the moving waters, which forms the beginning of the Edwards Aquifer. The river ultimately flows to a gorgeous lake impounded just down from the edge of the property.,,Location & Access,Easily accessed yet wonderfully secluded, the property lies in a prized corridor of the upper Guadalupe watershed, which is an area long revered for its clean water, dramatic terrain, and generational landholdings. A small portion of the ranch extends into Guadalupe Ranch Estates, granting the owner exclusive access to two additional private river parks featuring more limestone flats and deep, spring-fed swimming holes. Ranch road frontage is well maintained pavement, and 2-wheel drive vehicles suffice in arriving at the homestead.,,Landscape & Improvements,The land unfolds in a captivating blend of natural untouched tree-covered terrain, and purposeful enhancement and clearing. Cliffs rise above fern-lined springs, hiding caves while accessible, distant, panoramic views frame the horizon. Improvements are extensive and distinctive, including a custom waterslide, a one-of-a-kind bridge crossing, spring box, RV pad/patio, and multiple infrastructure elements designed for immediate use and enjoyment. An established homesite pad with power, water, and propane subbed in is already in place, ready for the foundation of a future main residence or lodge up near the headquarters.,,Water,Broken Halos River Ranch showcases over 1,600 feet of prized North Fork Guadalupe River frontage. Along these banks, thoughtfully crafted, park-like settings have been shaped and stabilized with hand-laid river rock retaining walls. The riverfront artfully balances natural characteristics with clever and thoughtful improvements, highlighted by an exceptional spring box where clear, life-giving water bubbles directly from out of the cliff.,,Near the river and within the heart of the ranch, numerous additional springs well up, placing this ranch as one of the sources of the rivers headwaters, which is a rare and highly sought after distinction in the Hill Country. Water infrastructure is also impressive, with two dedicated wells: one servicing the homes and improvements, and the other sustaining grass for livestock and wildlife while keeping a 30,000 gallon holding tank full, thats built to function as both a water reserve and a swimming pool.,,Wildlife & Recreation,The ranch is fully high-fenced and managed with longevity and quality in mind, supporting a diverse population of premier exotics including Red Stag, Fallow, Axis, Blackbuck, the occasional Aoudad, and highly improved whitetail genetics. An existing agricultural valuation is in place, made possible by a small herd of impressive Texas Longhorns and donkeys that are intended to convey.,,Summary,At the southern edge of the property sits a welcoming headquarters compound featuring two exceptional country cabins and an extraordinary outdoor entertaining area set at the beginning of sweeping, long-range views overlooking the bulk of your property and beyond. Just down from there, youll find a well-appointed shop with a walk-in cooler and game processing station, and the well, holding tanks, trough, feeders and gun range. The craftsmanship of the primary guest cabin is remarkable, while the secondary pre-fabricated residence is elevated and maintained to a standard rarely seen, making both ideal for weekend retreats or full-time living while a legacy home is envisioned.,,This offering is flowing over with both obvious and hidden details, each discovered only through time spent on the land. A property of this caliber, water quality, and improvement level is seldom available and must be experienced in person to be fully taken in. Private showings are available by appointment

listings.description_full: *LIVE AND ONLINE AUCTION*,,PROPERTY: 78.3 +/- Acres in Rice County, Kansas,,AUCTION DATE: October 6th, 2026 at 6 PM Central,,AUCTION LOCATION: Inman Community Building 406 E Center, Inman, KS 67546,Farm and Hunt Combination 80 near Little River,On behalf of the Mayo Family, L2 Realty presents an "80" of productive farm ground and recreational land south of Little River in Rice County, Kansas! Selling at auction on October 6th, this combination farm offers approximately 50 acres of tillable ground, 12 acres of native hay meadow, creek-bottom timber, and excellent blacktop road access. With income-producing cropland, native grass, and wooded wildlife habitat all packed into an affordable-sized tract, this property would make a great entry-level recreational farm, investment property, or addition to an existing farming operation.,Tillable Ground & Crop Production:,Approximately 50 acres of the property consist of tillable farm ground. Roughly 18 acres in the northwest portion of the farm are currently planted to soybeans, while approximately 32 additional acres recently came out of CRP and provide an opportunity to return more acreage to crop production.,,The tillable soils are primarily Class 2 and Class 3 loams. Average NCCPI of 63 across the whole farm with Clark clay loam, Saltcreek and Naron fine sandy loam, Lancaster loam, and Kipson loam. The crop ground will be open after harvest, with possession occurring after the current crop is harvested.,Native Hay & Grassland:,Approximately 12 acres of native grass are located in the northeast portion of the property and are currently being utilized for hay production. This area adds another productive component to the farm while also creating grassland habitat and additional edge for wildlife.,,Between the crop ground, native grass, timber, and creek corridor, the property has a diverse mix of land uses.,Creek, Timber & Wildlife Habitat:,A dry creek runs east to west through the center of the property and creates a natural travel corridor through the farm. Timber and brush associated with the drainage provide cover for whitetail deer and help funnel wildlife between neighboring agricultural fields and surrounding habitat. Check out the trail camera photos, there are a good number of quality bucks currently using this farm!,,During the rut, creek drainages like this can serve as natural cruising routes for bucks moving across the landscape. The wooded south and east boundaries provide additional cover, travel corridors, and clearly defined property lines.,,For someone looking to purchase their first recreational tract, this farm offers a nice combination of huntable cover and agricultural income without requiring the investment of a much larger recreational property. Whitetail deer and upland bird hunting opportunities add another dimension to an already productive piece of Kansas land.,Access:,Access is one of the strongest features of this property. The farm lies along a blacktop road, eliminating the concerns that can come with miles of gravel or minimum-maintenance roads during wet weather.,,An interior access road associated with the existing oil-production infrastructure runs through the property and provides convenient access across much of the farm. This road can also be useful for checking crops, accessing hunting locations, managing the property, or moving equipment throughout the tract.,Investment Opportunity:,This 80  acre tract offers several potential sources of agricultural value. Approximately 18 acres are already in active crop production, another 32  acres have recently come out of CRP, and approximately 12 acres are currently being used for native hay production.,,That combination makes the property attractive to several types of buyers. An investor can own recreational ground while generating agricultural income to help offset ownership costs. A beginning land buyer can step into a manageable-sized hunting and income property. Local farmers and landowners can add acreage to an existing operation while picking up additional recreational value at the same time.,Mineral Rights:,The property will sell surface rights only. Oil-production infrastructure is currently located on the farm, and the existing interior access road is utilized for servicing that infrastructure.,Location:,Located south of Little River in Rice County, Kansas, this property combines rural location with excellent year-round blacktop access. The surrounding agricultural landscape, creek drainage, native grass, and timber provide a strong mix for both farming and recreation.,, ,Property Highlights:,, Located south of Little River, Kansas in Rice County, Selling at auction October 6th, 2026, Approximately 12 acres of native grass currently utilized for hay production, Approximately 18 acres currently planted to soybeans, Approximately 32 acres recently released from CRP, Tillable soils consisting primarily of Class 2 and Class 3 clay loams and sandy loams, Possession after harvest, Dry creek running east to west through the center of the farm, Creek timber providing a natural whitetail travel corridor, Whitetail deer and upland bird hunting opportunities, Blacktop road frontage for excellent all-weather access, Interior access road running through much of the property, Surface rights only, sellers retaining all mineral rights,,,,Whether you're looking for productive acreage, an entry-level hunting farm, or another investment to add to your current land holdings, this Rice County combination farm fits a lot of needs. Crop income, native hay, wildlife habitat, and blacktop access create a versatile Kansas property with both agricultural and recreational value. Selling at auction October 6th, 2026. listings.description_full: This 154.232± acre offering in Warren County, Ohio brings together productive tillable cropland and wooded recreational ground in one property — tucked into a quiet, private setting in southwest Ohio, just south of Interstate 71 between Wilmington and Lebanon. Offered at live auction in six individual tracts, with both live in-person and online bidding, the land can be purchased as a single tract, in any combination of tracts, or in its entirety, giving farmers, investors, and recreational or lifestyle buyers the chance to tailor a purchase to their acreage and budget.,,,The open ground is genuinely workable, carrying level, productive soils — largely Clermont and Jonesboro-Rossmoyne silt loams — well suited to row-crop production. Interspersed with and bordering the cropland are stands of mature woods that add outstanding hunting, wildlife habitat, and natural cover, so a buyer can farm the tillable acres while holding timbered ground for recreation. The property also carries frontage on State Route 350 and State Route 22, providing strong access across the tracts; the corner tract alone offers 950 feet of frontage on State Route 350 and 1,170 feet on State Route 22.,,Because the land is enrolled in Ohio's Current Agricultural Use Valuation (CAUV) program, ownership comes with the benefit of reduced property taxes tied to agricultural use. Every tract is vacant and buildable, ready for its next chapter — whether that means expanding a farming operation, building a long-term land investment, putting up a home or cabin in a quiet country setting, or securing a private recreational retreat close to home in southwest Ohio.,,Tracts range from a compact, secluded wooded parcel ideal for hunting and quiet weekends to larger tracts of predominantly open cropland, offering an uncommon level of flexibility — and opportunity — for a single Warren County property. Property previews are Tuesday, October 20 and Tuesday, October 27 from 4:00 to 6:00 PM, and Saturday, November 7 from 10:00 AM to noon; interested buyers are encouraged to walk the tracts before auction day.,

listings.description_full: Auction Date: Thursday, November 19th, 2026 @ 10:00 AM,Auction Location: Beattie Community Building (307 Whiting) Beattie, KS,Sellers – Anthony & Elizabeth Ray Revocable Living Trust,Property Legal Description:,Tract 1: S32, T01, R09, ACRES 156.2, SW4 LESS R/W,Tract 2: S05, T02, R09, ACRES 155.7, NW4 LESS R/W,FSA Details:,Tract 1 (Estimated due to tracts being combined),155.44 Farmland Acres 112.83 DCP Cropland Acres,109.75 Base Acres (Soybeans 49.82 acres, Corn 38.07 acres, Wheat 21.86 acres),Tract 2 (Estimated due to tracts being combined),155.8 Farmland Acres 89.98 DCP Cropland Acres,87.65 Base Acres (Soybeans 39.78 acres, Corn 30.41 acres, Wheat 17.46 acres),Broker’s Notes:,From Buchanan Patent to Modern Production… A Rare Opportunity to Own Highly Productive Robidoux Creek Bottom Farms Rich in Kansas History.,Rich in history and unmatched in agricultural productivity, the Ray Family Trust presents a rare opportunity to purchase two outstanding farms in Marshall County, Kansas. Located directly across Frontier Road from one another, with Tract 1 situated on the north side and Tract 2 on the south, these highly productive farms have remained in the same family since the earliest days of Kansas settlement.,The history of these properties is truly remarkable. The land was originally deeded to the family’s ancestors by President James Buchanan during the settlement of this region of Kansas, making these farms part of the area’s earliest private ownership. Long before modern roads existed, the historic Military Trail crossed this area, following a route very near present-day Frontier Road. The legendary Pony Express also traveled this corridor, with riders changing horses at the nearby Guittard Station, Few properties offer such a unique combination of historical significance and long-standing family ownership.,Beyond their rich heritage, these farms are exceptional agricultural investments. Both tracts feature highly fertile Robidoux Creek bottom soils that have consistently produced outstanding crops for generations. The productive creek bottom, combined with excellent soil composition, makes these farms ideal additions for operators seeking quality acreage with proven performance. Continuous corn and soybean rotations have demonstrated the productivity and dependability of these farms.,In addition to their farming potential, both properties offer outstanding recreational appeal. The timbered creek corridors and natural travel routes create excellent habitat for whitetail deer and wild turkey, providing exceptional hunting opportunities while maintaining productive farming operations. This balance of income-producing cropland and quality wildlife habitat is increasingly difficult to find.,Tract 1 Highlights:,,• 112.62 +/- acres of productive cropland.,• Approximately 63% Class II soils.,• Highly productive Robidoux Creek bottom farmland.,• Proven history of corn and soybean production.,• Excellent combination of income-producing cropland and wildlife habitat.,Tract 2 Highlights:,,• 87.12 +/- acres of productive cropland.,• Approximately 68% Class II soils.,• Fertile bottom ground with outstanding agricultural capability.,• Strong recreational appeal with abundant deer and turkey habitat.,• Historic location along the former Military Trail and near the original Guittard Station Pony Express route.,Whether your objective is expanding a farming operation, investing in premium tillable land, or owning a property with extraordinary historical significance and recreational value, the Ray Family Trust farms represent an exceptional opportunity. It is rare to find two neighboring tracts that combine proven agricultural productivity, abundant wildlife, and a legacy dating back to the earliest settlement of Kansas. These farms have been carefully stewarded by the same family for generations and are now available for new ownership to continue that tradition.,Property Location:,From Beattie, KS: From Hwy 99 & Ironstone Road (Elm Street) intersection travel west on Ironstone Road (Elm Street) for .5 miles to 21st Road then travel north on 21st Road for 3.5 miles to Frontier Road then travel west on Frontier Road for .5 miles to the properties. listings.description_short: Exclusive South Fork river frontage with legendary trout fishing, panoramic mountain views, a luxury residence, private pond, and exceptional recreational amenities.
listings.description_full: 141 acre ranch featuring approximately 1 mile of South Fork of the Snake River frontage with exclusive access to the renowned Powerline Ripple. This extraordinary property offers world-class trout fishing, breathtaking mountain views, and a custom 3-bedroom, 5-bath home with vaulted ceilings, a dramatic river rock fireplace, floor-to-ceiling windows, a gourmet kitchen, private pond, barn, and abundant wildlife in a remarkable setting. ,,Land ,,Stunning 141 acre riverfront estate positioned along the coveted South Fork of the Snake River in Swan Valley, Idaho, with the majestic Baldy Mountain providing a breathtaking backdrop. World-class fly fishing awaits just beyond your doorstep, including exclusive access to the renowned Powerline Ripple, one of the river’s most celebrated fishing runs. Widely recognized as one of North America’s premier trout fisheries, the South Fork is famed for its abundant rainbow, cutthroat, and brown trout, delivering an unparalleled angling experience amid the breathtaking scenery of eastern Idaho.,For the discerning outdoorsman, private river frontage on the South Fork of the Snake River represents a rare opportunity to own a piece of one of Idaho’s most coveted recreational landscapes--where exceptional fishing, solitude, and natural beauty converge at your doorstep.,The irrigated farm ground is actively maintained by a local producer, ensuring productive, well-kept fields that enhance the property’s beauty while providing an excellent food source and habitat for abundant wildlife.,A conservation easement safeguards this extraordinary ranch in perpetuity, preserving its pristine natural beauty, abundant wildlife, and open landscapes while creating a lasting legacy for future generations.,,141.49 acres,Picturesque river setting with panoramic mountain views featuring the prominent Baldy Mountain,Year-round access is provided by a county-maintained road plowed to the driveway, offering reliable access,Adjacent to National Forest,Attached 2-car Garage,Restored barn, storage shed, garden space, and fenced acreage,Mature landscape,Private fishing pond fed by Indian Creek,Water rights,(2) 1,000-gallon buried propane tanks,Abundant wildlife  moose, elk, deer, and more,World-class trout fishing is yours to enjoy with direct access to the South Fork of the Snake River and the iconic Powerline Ripple,,,,Improvements ,,This exceptional property offers a custom 4,536 square foot residence where refined craftsmanship, timeless design, and the surrounding natural landscape come together in perfect harmony. The thoughtfully designed floor plan includes three bedrooms, five bathrooms, and an expansive upstairs loft/bonus room complete with its own bathroom, providing an elegant yet comfortable retreat for everyday living and entertaining.,Architectural details throughout the home reflect a commitment to quality and character, with soaring vaulted ceilings, hand-selected solid wood beam accents, rustic designer lighting, and rich tongue-and-groove finishes creating a warm and inviting ambiance. The great room serves as the centerpiece of the residence, featuring a dramatic floor-to-ceiling river rock gas insert fireplace with a substantial log beam mantel. Expansive windows frame breathtaking views of the South Fork of the Snake River, surrounding mountains, and neighboring National Forest lands, bringing the beauty of the outdoors seamlessly inside.,The home’s exceptional entertaining spaces extend into the formal dining area and adjoining wet bar, featuring marble countertops, built-in display cabinetry, a wine refrigerator, and an ice maker. This thoughtfully appointed space provides an inviting setting for intimate gatherings or memorable occasions with family and guests.,The gourmet kitchen blends functionality with refined style, offering custom cabinetry with abundant storage, granite countertops, a built-in hutch, and an oversized marble island with built-in breakfast bar. Additional appointments include tile flooring, double oven range, a wall oven featuring a convection microwave, a built-in overlay refrigerator, pantry, reverse osmosis system, trash compactor and a built-in workspace--creating a highly functional culinary environment suited for both everyday living and entertaining.,The private primary suite offers a tranquil retreat overlooking the river, with French doors opening to the patio and providing seamless access to the outdoor living spaces. The suite features a cozy sitting area, stone-inlay gas insert fireplace, and a spa-inspired bathroom appointed with dual vanities, a large jetted soaking tub, and a steam walk-in shower, creating a serene sanctuary designed for relaxation and comfort.,Two additional guest suites, each with a private bathroom, provide comfort and privacy for family and guests. A spacious laundry and mudroom enhance the home’s functionality, while the second-floor loft/bonus room with private bathroom offers flexible living space ideal for a home office, media room, game room, or additional guest accommodations.,Exceptional attention to quality, comfort, and peace of mind is evident throughout the home’s thoughtfully curated improvements. The home is equipped with hydronic radiant heat and forced air cooling with humidity control, providing exceptional comfort and climate efficiency in every season. A state-of-the-art integrated security system provides intelligent monitoring for intrusion, fire, and water detection, delivering comprehensive protection for the residence. Significant recent upgrades include a premium composite roof, expansive rear decking, new concrete walkways, and a covered patio that extends the home’s inviting outdoor living spaces. Additional enhancements, including a professionally sealed crawl space and an energy-efficient tankless water heater, further reflect the property’s commitment to lasting quality, efficiency, and low-maintenance ownership., Every detail of this exceptional residence has been thoughtfully curated to provide a sophisticated mountain-river lifestyle, offering the perfect blend of luxury, comfort, and connection to the extraordinary landscape that surrounds it.,,,Recreation ,,The Swan Valley region is a true outdoor paradise, offering endless opportunities for recreation surrounded by rugged mountain landscapes, pristine waterways, and abundant wildlife. The famed South Fork of the Snake River flows through the valley and is renowned as one of the premier fly-fishing destinations in the West, attracting anglers from around the world for its exceptional trout fishing, scenic float trips, and breathtaking river corridors. Beyond the river, the area provides unparalleled access to hiking, horseback riding, hunting, wildlife viewing, boating, camping, and winter recreation, all set against the backdrop of the Snake River Range, Palisades, and surrounding National Forest lands.,,,Agriculture ,,The property is irrigated by twobrand-new pivots and a wheel line irrigation system, enhancing productivity and providing efficient water management across the property.,,,Water/Mineral Rights & Natural Resources ,,Approximately 1 mile of frontage along the legendary South Fork of the Snake River,Indian Creek meanders through the property, enhancing the landscape, and attracting abundant wildlife,Private pond fed by Indian Creek, enhancing the property’s natural beauty and wildlife habitat,Valuable water rights include Water Right 23-67C for irrigation and Water Right 23-67D for recreation storage,A rare combination of river frontage, Indian Creek, and private pond creates exceptional water resources and habitat diversity,Protected by a conservation easement, the property’s natural landscape is preserved in perpetuity,,,,Region & Climate ,,Swan Valley enjoys a beautiful four-season mountain climate with warm, comfortable summers, crisp autumns, snowy winters, and refreshing springs. Summer days typically reach the upper 70s to low 80s with cool evenings, making outdoor recreation enjoyable throughout the season. Winters bring reliable snowfall and picturesque mountain scenery, while spring and fall offer mild temperatures and vibrant seasonal color. The area’s higher elevation provides fresh mountain air, low humidity, and distinct seasons.,,,History ,,Swan Valley has a rich history deeply rooted in agriculture, ranching, and the natural resources that define eastern Idaho. Originally inhabited by the Shoshone-Bannock and other Native American tribes, the valley later became a corridor for early explorers, trappers, and settlers drawn to the fertile lands and abundant waterways. Over generations, ranching, farming, and outdoor traditions have shaped the community and remain central to the area’s identity today. The valley’s close proximity to Jackson Hole, the Greater Yellowstone Ecosystem, and extensive public lands provides a rare combination of seclusion, recreation, and accessibility. Known for its scenic beauty, wildlife habitat, and legendary South Fork of the Snake River, Swan Valley continues to attract those seeking a connection to Idaho’s rugged landscapes and Western heritage. Serving as a gateway to world-class outdoor recreation, including fishing, boating, hiking, wildlife viewing, snow sports and easy access to nearby national forests and the greater Yellowstone region.,,,Location ,,Swan Valley is a scenic rural community in eastern Idaho, located in Bonneville County along the renowned South Fork of the Snake River. Situated at an elevation of approximately 5,300 feet, the valley lies between the Snake River Range and the Caribou-Targhee National Forest, offering a stunning backdrop of forested mountains, open meadows, and pristine waterways. Ideally positioned just northeast of Idaho Falls and within close proximity to Jackson Hole and the Greater Yellowstone region, Swan Valley provides convenient access to world-class fly fishing, boating, hiking, hunting, and year-round outdoor recreation.,The landscape is defined by broad river valleys framed by forested foothills and rugged mountain ridges, with expansive meadows, sagebrush flats, wetlands, and rich riparian corridors along the South Fork of the Snake River. The area is surrounded by an abundance of natural resources, including rivers, streams, reservoirs, and alpine lakes, creating exceptional opportunities for fishing, wildlife viewing, horseback riding, and exploring Idaho’s backcountry.,Swan Valley offers accessibility, with convenient access to regional airports, nearby communities, and everyday amenities. The property is approximately 40 miles northeast of Idaho Falls, providing access to shopping, dining, medical services, and regional conveniences. Idaho Falls Regional Airport (IDA) is the closest commercial airport, offering daily flights and connections throughout the West. The world-renowned destinations of Jackson Hole, Wyoming, and Grand Teton National Park are approximately 60 miles away, providing access to additional amenities, recreation, and travel connections. Nearby communities including Swan Valley, Irwin, Ririe, and Idaho Falls offer a variety of services, while the greater Jackson Hole and Yellowstone regions provide exceptional dining, entertainment, and outdoor experiences.,Nearby Access:,,Idaho Falls, ID  ~40 miles | Regional airport, shopping, dining, healthcare, and services,Jackson Hole, WY  ~60 miles | World-class recreation, dining, lodging, and commercial airport,Grand Teton National Park  ~5565 miles | Iconic mountain landscapes and outdoor recreation,Yellowstone National Park  ~100 miles | National Park access and year-round adventure,Idaho Falls Regional Airport (IDA)  ~40 miles | Commercial air service and connections

listings.title: Henry’s Fork Snake River Ranch
listings.types_label: Recreational Property, Riverfront Property, Waterfront Property, House
listings.description_short: Legacy ranch offering world-class fishing, premier hunting, productive farmland, and scenic water features in a coveted recreational corridor.
listings.description_full: Henry’s Fork Snake River Ranch  A Legacy Recreational and Agricultural Estate in Eastern Idaho.,Along the legendary Henry’s Fork of the Snake River near Rexburg, Idaho, this rare and remarkably expansive 1,048 acre legacy ranch combines the best of productive farmland, world-class fishing, recreation, rich waterfowl habitat and well-appointed improvementsall set against the scenic beauty of one of the West’s most coveted riverfront flyways.,,Land ,,Located just outside of Rexburg, Henry’s Fork Snake River Ranch is a sanctuary of natural beauty and productivity. Spanning 1,048 deeded acres, it offers an impressive 500 acres of highly productive cropland, with approximately 400 acres under pivots and the rest under side rollssupported by robust water rights, delivering strong agricultural output season after season. The remaining land within the ranch is sub-irrigated, providing additional production potential.The landscape of this expansive ranch is defined by its gentle topography and rich, diverse features creating a landscape that is functional and scenic.,The ranch’s crown jewels are its abundant water features. Over four miles of live water weave through the property, creating a haven for wildlife and aquatic life alike. This includes over half a mile of the Bannock Jim Slough, nearly 1.5 miles of the Texas Slough, and just over two miles of the Henry’s Fork Snake River (Cartier Slough). In addition, the Texas Slough Canal also traverses through the property, enhancing irrigation and enriching the natural water system. These waterways create lush riparian corridors lined with mature cottonwoods and willows, adding habitat diversity and striking beauty.,With direct frontage on the Henry’s Fork and several scenic sloughs winding through the property, this former duck club delivers world-class trout fishing, premier waterfowl and big game hunting, and an unmatched connection to Idaho’s renowned outdoor heritage.,Bordering the Cartier Slough Wildlife Management Area, the property benefits from direct adjacency to public lands, ensuring privacy and supporting an already thriving wildlife presence. The combination of river frontage, slough systems, and fertile ground make Henry’s Fork Snake River Ranch a standout for both natural beauty and agricultural productivity.,In addition to its striking natural features and agricultural strength, the ranch is enhanced by a variety of well-appointed improvements and residences, suited for both comfort and day-to-day operations.,,,Improvements ,,This exceptional ranch features two comfortable residences, including a spacious 3-bedroom, 2-bath home and a charming 2-bedroom, 1-bath dwelling, perfect for family, guests, or ranch staff. The property is enhanced by a variety of improvements featuring an impressive two-bay barn complete with stables and generous space for equipment and tack, plus an immaculate workshop with a convenient loft, offering plenty of room for projects and storage. Additional improvements include a detached two-door garage, a large hay shed, multiple sets of state-of-the-art pipe-fenced working corrals, and various other outbuildings. These well-maintained facilities blend comfortable living with practical day-to-day ranch operations and agricultural use.,,,Recreation ,,The region surrounding Henry’s Fork Snake River Ranch offers access to some of the most celebrated outdoor recreation in the West, much of it within two hours or less from the property. Whether you’re an avid hunter, angler, hiker, or simply enjoy exploring the outdoors, the opportunities are both abundant and diverse!,For hunters, eastern Idaho is known for exceptional big game and upland bird hunting. The ranch itself offers strong waterfowl and mule deer opportunities, and nearby public lands expand access to elk, whitetail, and other species. Anglers will find world-renowned fly fishing in every direction, particularly on the Henry’s Fork, which runs along the ranch’s edge, and the nearby South Fork of the Snake River, both renowned for healthy populations of rainbow, brown, and cutthroat trout.,For hikers, off-roaders, and nature lovers, the landscape opens up with endless terrain to explore. The iconic Menan Buttes, ancient volcanic craters, offer scenic trails and sweeping views, just 20 minutes away from the ranch. Henry’s Fork Snake River Ranch is also within close reach of the Targhee National Forest, providing miles of trails for hiking, mountain biking, horseback riding, snowmobiling, and ATV use. Off-roading enthusiasts will also appreciate the vast network of BLM roads and backcountry routes across the region.,A scenic 90-minute drive brings you to the entrance of Yellowstone National Park, where towering peaks, alpine lakes, and world-class wildlife viewing await. Grand Teton National Park is also just under two hours from the ranch, placing one of America’s most iconic natural wonders within easy reach for day trips.,For more relaxed outings, downtown Rexburg offers charming local shops, dining, and seasonal events. The nearby cities of Idaho Falls, ID and Jackson, WY provide additional cultural attractions, restaurants, and outdoor outfitters. Whether it’s casting a fly, glassing for elk and deer, or exploring one of America’s most scenic national parks, Henry’s Fork Snake River Ranch offers unrivaled access to the heart of the Rocky Mountain West!,,,Location ,,Henry’s Fork Snake River Ranch benefits from a prime location in eastern Idaho, offering both the seclusion of a private rural setting and the convenience of nearby amenities. The property is situated less than 20 minutes west of Rexburg, a vibrant and growing community with a wide array of services. In Rexburg, locals and guests will find all essential amenities including grocery stores, hardware and agricultural supply outlets, restaurants, medical clinics, and Madison Memorial Hospital, a full-service healthcare facility. The town is also home to Brigham Young UniversityIdaho, contributing to a well-supported local economy and a lively cultural scene.,For those in need of air travel, the ranch is located just 35 minutes from Idaho Falls Regional Airport, which provides regular domestic flights and car rental services. Pocatello Regional Airport, offering additional travel options, is located less than 90 minutes to the south.,Beyond Rexburg, the surrounding region includes several other accessible communities such as Idaho Falls, Rigby, and St. Anthony, all offering additional shopping, dining, healthcare, and recreational amenities. The ranch’s location strikes an ideal balance between peaceful rural living and convenient access to regional hubs, making it well-suited for both year-round living and seasonal retreat.

listings.description_full: Kinney Ranch – 258.2± Deeded Acres | 235± Irrigated Acres | Blackfoot, Idaho,,Exclusive listing with Keller Williams Realty East Idaho — Listing Agent Scott Chappell, with Farmland Company Real Estate LLC serving as marketing partner.,,Kinney Ranch is a highly productive, asset-class agricultural property located near Blackfoot, Idaho, offering a rare combination of scale, water security, and proven income history. This turnkey operation spans 258.2± total deeded acres, with 235± irrigated acres under pipe, positioning it as a premium acquisition for expanding regional operators or agricultural portfolio investors seeking a farm with demonstrated production history.,Irrigation,,The farm is fully irrigated via two Valley center pivot irrigation systems, equipped with FieldNET remote monitoring and control, allowing the operator to manage pivot operation, monitor performance, and make adjustments directly from a smartphone. Water is supplied by a irrigation well with pump and Variable Frequency Drive (VFD), delivering efficient, reliable water at a controlled rate. The farm's water position is backed by three adjudicated groundwater rights, all decreed and active, with a senior priority date of 1951 — a significant asset in Idaho's groundwater administration system, providing strong seniority in the Eastern Snake Plain Aquifer.,,Soils & Production History,The property is comprised predominantly of high-yielding Pancheri silt loam soils, supporting a proven crop rotation of potatoes, sugar beets, wheat, alfalfa, and barley. The farm has been actively and precisely managed, with documented GPS-guided fertilizer application records confirming consistent, data-driven agronomic practices across the operation.,,Access & Layout,Kinney Ranch features a clean, efficient layout with excellent year-round access directly along North 700 West Road, simplifying equipment movement and operational logistics.,,With senior water rights, modern remote-controlled irrigation infrastructure, and productive soils, Kinney Ranch is built for consistent, high-value specialty and row-crop production — a compelling opportunity for operators and investors alike.,Water Rights Detail:,,35-14528 — Priority 2/24/1953  ,35-14529 — Priority 6/7/1957 ,35-14527 — Priority 8/4/1979 ,,Location: Lemhi Road, Blackfoot, ID 83221 (Bingham County),Price: $2,194,955,Size: 258.23± Acres,For more information or to schedule a showing, contact:,Scott Chappell, Listing Broker,Keller Williams Realty East Idaho,208-268-3968

listings.description_full: Set in the heart of Southeast Iowas highly regarded White Elm neighborhood, the Barnhart Farm is the kind of legacy property that has been built through numerous transactions across two decades. Located among the rolling white oak hills near Douds, Eldon, Floris, and Selma, this farm sits in a proven region near the Des Moines River, which is known for exceptional whitetails generation after generation. The landscape captures everything people love about Southern Iowa massive oak ridges, hidden creek bottoms, scenic views, and a timeless feel thats become increasingly difficult to find. From massive historic oak and hedge trees to the quiet draws and hardwood hillsides, the property carries a character and presence that immediately stands out. Access is a major strength of the farm. With dead-end road access from the east, a west entrance that brings you to the hilltop cabin, and an additional discreet southwest access point, the property offers exceptional stealth with minimal road frontage, but great access throughout a rare combination for a farm of this size. The habitat is ideal for mature whitetails, with big ridge systems, thick cover, and five separate drainages feeding into a creek in the middle of the farm. It supports high deer numbers and provides the type of terrain where bucks can comfortably live, bed, and remain patternable throughout much of the season. During the late season, food sources can draw in additional bucks from surrounding areas, creating excellent winter hunting opportunities. Several proven stand and blind sites have consistently produced quality hunts over the years. Established tower blinds overlook key bedding areas, green plots, and strategic travel corridors, while the farms expansive layout also allows for an enjoyable run-and-gun style bowhunting experience. The diversity of setups gives hunters the ability to adapt to varying wind directions and seasonal movement patterns. Water is another standout feature, with 3 fishing ponds, 7 additional water holes and small ponds, and 5 branches supplying a creek throughout the property. These resources not only enhance wildlife habitat but also add to the farms overall recreational appeal. Timber value also adds long-term investment potential. Approximately seven years ago, the property received a significant select-cut timber bid of $190,000, though the owners elected not to harvest, leaving the next owner with an impressive stand of mature hardwoods. Sitting in the perfect spot, the hilltop cabin offers outstanding views without interfering with the farms hunting. The setup includes rural water, electricity, septic, and a storage shop, creating a comfortable basecamp for hunting season or weekend retreats. Beyond the land itself, the surrounding neighborhood is known for quality deer management and cooperative relationships among neighboring landowners. Shared trail camera information and a focus on age management help contribute to the areas reputation as one of Southeast Iowas premier hunting regions. The Barnhart Farm is more than just a hunting property its the kind of place built around tradition, family memories, and the pursuit of mature whitetails in some of Iowas best habitat. For more information on this exceptional farm, contact Ben Harshyne or Hersh Smith with The Southeast Iowa Land Team at Whitetail Properties Real Estate.

listings.description_full: Welcome to an exceptional 1,050 acre turnkey hunting property with a 4,650 sq ft lodge in the heart of Tensas Parish, Louisianaan area widely recognized for producing trophy whitetails and unforgettable waterfowl seasons. Located just one-quarter mile from the renowned Tensas National Wildlife Refuge and only a quarter mile from the Tensas River, this property sits in a prime big buck corridor within a proven duck flyway. Surrounded by rich agricultural ground, the combination of habitat diversity and neighboring food sources creates ideal conditions for growing and holding mature whitetails, attracting migrating waterfowl, and supporting a strong turkey population. A majority of the property is in WRE and has a great stand of 28-year-old planted hardwoods, with most in a variety of Oak trees. The lodge has been recently updated and is designed for both comfort and entertaining. Featuring 7 bedrooms and 5.5 bathrooms, it offers ample space for family, friends, or corporate guests. A screened-in outdoor cooking area provides the perfect setting to gather after the hunt and enjoy the peaceful surroundings. Supporting improvements include a large metal equipment shed with a walk-in cooler, allowing you to store machinery and properly care for harvested game easily. For the deer hunter, the property is fully equipped with 10 elevated Redneck fiberglass blinds strategically positioned over 10 established food plots, offering turnkey setups and excellent visibility. The area is known for producing quality, mature bucks, and this tract is no exception. This area is known for killing deer over 150 inches. For waterfowl enthusiasts, the improved duck holes feature new levees and water-control structures, along with approximately 150 acres of potential low-water areas that can be managed to create optimal duck habitat. The thoughtful water management infrastructure provides flexibility to plant, flood, and hold ducks throughout the season. The internal road system is top-notch and truck-ready when things are dry. With convenient highway frontage, premier improvements, and a location surrounded by agriculture in one of Louisianas most sought-after hunting regions, this property is a rare opportunity to own a fully developed recreational tract offering outstanding deer, duck, and turkey hunting all in one package.
